title: compiler-aliases: Wire save=set and do=run aliases through parser + digester
description: Feature P1-7. Master §45 lists the canonical StepPrimitive variants. The YAML user-facing surface includes `save:` (alias for `set:`) and `do:` (alias for `run:`) per master §75 explain output examples (which show step kinds as `do`). vb_compile/src/mod_compile_lowering/part_02.rs:28-101 lower_canonical_step matches 10 of 12 StepPrimitive variants; Save and Do hit the `other` arm and return UnsupportedStepPrimitive. canonical_primitive_name in part_05.rs:98-114 maps Save→'save' and Set→'set' to different strings. digest_step_primitive in part_05.rs:374-381 writes distinct digest bytes. The result: a workflow using `save:` is rejected at compile time, and a workflow using `do:` followed by an equivalent `set:` would have a different digest (cache miss). This bead normalizes parser-level: when the YAML key is `save`, fold to Set{output, value}; when it's `do`, fold to Run. It also makes digest_step_primitive produce the same bytes for Save as for Set (identity).

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL accept both `save:` and `set:` YAML keys as equivalent (parser-level alias)
THE SYSTEM SHALL produce identical WorkflowDigests for workflows that differ only in `save` vs `set` (digest-level identity)

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a workflow YAML contains `save: { output: $x, value: ... }`
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL compile to the same CompiledNodeKind::SetConst as if the author wrote `set: { output: $x, value: ... }`

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a workflow YAML contains `do: { action: ..., input: ... }`
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL compile to the same CompiledNodeKind::Do as if the author wrote `run: { action: ..., input: ... }`

unwanted.condition: IF a workflow mixes `save:` and `set:` for the same logical step across versions
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT produce different WorkflowDigests
unwanted.because: Master §44.13 Fjall stores compiled IR keyed by ir_digest; cache misses waste recompute and break in-flight runs

preconditions: YAML parses under the strict profile (no anchors, no merge keys, single document)
Step key is one of the supported aliases: set, save, run, do
postconditions: CompiledNodeKind enum is the canonical form (SetConst, Do); aliases are stripped during lowering
WorkflowDigest of `save:` workflow == WorkflowDigest of equivalent `set:` workflow (byte-equal)
invariants: Alias normalization is idempotent: normalizing an already-normalized key returns the same key
Digest stability: same input, same digest, regardless of which alias the author used

happy: save_alias_compiles_to_set_const: `vb validate` on a workflow with `save: { output: $x, value: 42 }` succeeds; IR has SetConst node
do_alias_compiles_to_do_node: `vb validate` on a workflow with `do: { action: github.issue.create, input: $x }` succeeds; IR has Do node
save_and_set_produce_equal_digests: two workflows identical except for `save:` vs `set:` have the same WorkflowDigest
error: unknown_step_primitive_returns_unsupported: a workflow with `frobnicate: ...` fails to compile with UnsupportedStepPrimitive
edge: save_alias_in_nested_step_still_normalized: a Collect body with `save:` normalizes the same as top-level

files: crates/vb_compile/src/mod_compile_lowering/part_02.rs:28-101 (lower_canonical_step; the `other` arm catches Save and Do)
crates/vb_yaml/src/ast/parse_steps.rs (is_primitive function; where the parser-level normalization goes)
crates/vb_core/src/workflow/types.rs (StepPrimitive enum: Set, Save, Run, Do variants)
patterns: Pattern: existing alias normalization in parse_steps.rs (e.g., `then:` → `next:` per master §33)
Pattern: existing digest byte computation uses BLAKE3 keyed on the canonical primitive name
questions: Should the alias be applied at the AST level (parse_steps.rs) or at the lowering level (part_02.rs)? (Spec: AST level — gives consistent digests.)

Does the digest computation need to keep the Save variant in its enum, or can Save be removed entirely from StepPrimitive? (Spec: keep Save as an identity alias in the enum; remove its distinct digest bytes.)

security_failures.failure: An attacker exploits the alias to smuggle a `save:` step that bypasses a deny-list compiled against `set:` steps
security_failures.prevention: After alias normalization, the IR is identical; deny-lists operate on the IR, not the YAML surface

usability_failures.failure: Workflow author uses `save:` and gets a confusing `UnsupportedStepPrimitive: Save` error
usability_failures.prevention: Parser-level normalization accepts both; error is never surfaced

data_integrity_failures.failure: A workflow in version 1 uses `set:`, version 2 uses `save:`; both are semantically identical but have different digests, fragmenting the compiled IR cache
data_integrity_failures.prevention: Digest is computed on the normalized form, so both versions share a digest
data_integrity_failures.test_for_it: save_and_set_produce_equal_digests (assert BLAKE3 hash bytes are equal)

integration_failures.failure: An external tool that reads the YAML source to extract step types gets confused by the alias
integration_failures.prevention: Tool consumes the IR (canonical), not the YAML source; if it reads YAML, normalize first
integration_failures.test_for_it: ir_does_not_contain_save_keyword (assert CompiledNodeKind::SetConst is the only form in the IR)

phase_2: In vb_yaml/src/ast/parse_steps.rs is_primitive: add a normalization step: if the YAML key is `save`, return StepPrimitive::Set{...} with the same body; if the key is `do`, return StepPrimitive::Do
In vb_compile/src/mod_compile_lowering/part_05.rs digest_step_primitive: remove the Save arm or keep it as an identity (same bytes as Set)
In vb_compile/src/mod_compile_lowering/part_02.rs lower_canonical_step: remove the `other` arm's UnsupportedStepPrimitive for Save (it's now normalized away)
phase_3: Update master §33 example YAMLs to show `save:` and `do:` as the recommended user-facing aliases
phase_4: Run `moon run :test -p vb_compile -p vb_yaml` and verify all new tests pass
Manual: `vb validate fixtures/save_alias.yaml && vb digest fixtures/save_alias.yaml` should match `vb digest fixtures/set_equivalent.yaml`

similar_implementations: Parser-level alias normalization in parse_steps.rs for `then:` → `next:` (master §33)
external_references: Master §75 explain output uses `do` as the kind label
